title: Automated Legacy Codebase Migration
business: Enterprise software firms managing massive, multi-decade legacy codebases.
problem: Manual refactoring of monolithic legacy systems is error-prone, costly, and often stalls due to the sheer volume of interdependencies that exceed standard context windows.
solution: Claude Opus 5.5 utilizes a 1M token context window and adaptive thinking to analyze entire repository structures, allowing it to perform complex refactoring tasks while maintaining architectural consistency across long-running agentic sessions.
steps: Ingest the entire legacy codebase into the 1M token context window.
Initialize the agentic loop using the claude-opus-5-5 model ID.
Configure the display setting to ensure progress updates are captured from thinking blocks.
Execute iterative refactoring tasks using the adaptive thinking capability to resolve interdependencies.
Validate output against the original system architecture.
outcome: A more maintainable, modular codebase achieved through automated, context-aware refactoring that preserves business logic integrity.
limitation: The model's adaptive thinking is always enabled, which can introduce latency; developers must monitor the display setting to ensure streaming progress updates are visible between tool calls.
